mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved by 7.4 percentage points from t-2w to t-0w, indicating a consistent upward trend. This momentum will persist over the next four weeks as consumers continue gradual return to retail venues, driving RETAIL_REC higher than the prior 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -72.0 to -64.6 over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean, or declines by more than 5 percentage points in any single week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has stabilized near -59%, indicating commuting patterns are not deteriorating further. When transit stabilizes above -65%, retail recovery accelerates because workers return to office-adjacent shopping. RETAIL_REC will rise over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains above -65% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -59.1 in t-0w, highest in four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT falls below -62% in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines from t-0w baseline.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC move together because both depend on willingness to leave home. When GROCERY_PHARM rises (currently -31.4, up from -39.4), it signals reduced infection fear. This behavioral shift drives concurrent RETAIL_REC gains over the next four weeks through reduced avoidance behavior.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises more than 3 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 7.5 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC diverge by more than 10 percentage points over the next four weeks, or both decline from t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES remains depressed at -53.1%, indicating remote work policies remain in effect. If WORKPLACES does not rise above -45% within two weeks, retail will remain suppressed because office-based foot traffic is absent. RETAIL_REC will decline or stagnate.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES fails to rise above -45% within two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES stable at -53% to -54% across all four weeks
regime_hint: tightening restrictions or sustained remote work mandate
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -40% and RETAIL_REC simultaneously increases by more than 5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has remained depressed at -58.7%, indicating outdoor activity avoidance persists. When PARKS stays below -55%, consumers substitute indoor retail for outdoor recreation. However, if PARKS begins rising sharply, consumers redirect spending to outdoor venues, reducing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 8 percentage points in any single week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -58.7 in t-0w, stable across four weeks
regime_hint: seasonal warming or policy reopening of outdoor spaces
failure_condition: PARKS remains below -55% and RETAIL_REC declines, or PARKS rises but RETAIL_REC also rises by more than 3 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 20.0 to 17.4 percentage points above baseline, indicating people are leaving home more frequently. This outbound mobility trend, combined with RETAIL_REC's recent improvement, signals sustained consumer activity. RETAIL_REC will continue rising over the next four weeks as home-leaving accelerates.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declining from 20.0 to 17.4 indicates increased outbound mobility
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rises above 20% or RETAIL_REC declines despite RESIDENTIAL falling below 15%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both severely depressed (-59.1 and -53.1 respectively), indicating coordinated avoidance of public spaces. If both remain below -50% for the next week, this signals sustained behavioral caution that will suppress RETAIL_REC recovery. RETAIL_REC will decline or remain flat over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -50% for one week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -59.1 and WORKPLACES at -53.1 in t-0w
regime_hint: tightening restrictions or sustained public health crisis
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES rises above -45% within one week, and RETAIL_REC simultaneously increases by more than 4 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has improved 7.5 points from t-2w to t-0w while RETAIL_REC improved only 7.4 points, indicating essential shopping is recovering faster than discretionary retail. This divergence signals policy prioritizes essential venues. If GROCERY_PHARM continues outpacing RETAIL_REC, retail restrictions remain in place and RETAIL_REC will decline relative to the prior 28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises more than 2 percentage points faster than RETAIL_REC week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC improvements are nearly equal but GROCERY_PHARM remains less suppressed
regime_hint: tightening restrictions with selective retail closures
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises faster than GROCERY_PHARM in any week, or both series converge within 5 percentage points.
